title: Restart Cascade: A Database Blip Kills Every Pod
businessContext: A Kubernetes API deployment uses the same /health endpoint for readiness and liveness. The endpoint queries PostgreSQL. A short database slowdown marks every pod unhealthy and starts synchronized restarts.
problemStatement: The API fleet restarts repeatedly during a database slowdown, although process health and CPU were normal before the restarts. Work through three timed developments, justify your actions, and write an evidence-based incident response. The simulation starts paused; advancing time can expire unanswered decisions.
constraints: Keep application deadlock detection; do not permanently disable all health checks.
Protect the database from reconnect storms.
Validate a canary before rolling out the new probe policy.
All telemetry is synthetic. Actions only affect this practice simulation.
candidateTasks: Contain customer impact while preserving evidence and data integrity.
Respond to each new development and explain the selected action.
Cite telemetry supporting the root cause; distinguish observation from inference.
Define a permanent correction, regression coverage, recovery gates, and stakeholder update.

stages.title: Dependency failure becomes process failure
stages.briefing: A 2-second database delay exceeds the 1-second probe timeout. All pods restart, then open new database pools at the same time.

branches.effective: The fleet stops treating dependency latency as proof that every process is dead.

stages.title: New pods need startup time
stages.briefing: The canary takes 45 seconds to initialize. Its liveness probe starts after 5 seconds, so it is killed before startup finishes.

branches.effective: The running fleet is stable; fix initialization checks without rushing replacement pods.
branches.partial: Some impact remains. Keep the old healthy replicas serving while removing the restart cascade.
branches.harmful: Keep the old healthy replicas serving while removing the restart cascade.

hints: Liveness failures explicitly cite SELECT 1 timeout despite normal pre-failure CPU.
Roll back the probe change to the last verified policy; retain healthy replicas and bound reconnect retries.
Provide distinct startup, liveness and readiness semantics with thresholds based on measured behavior.
alternativeApproaches: For a service that can serve useful cached reads, keep those paths available while explicitly degrading writes.
For a service unable to serve any safe request without the database, readiness may depend on it, with thresholds and recovery behavior tested.
commonMistakes: Making liveness query every shared dependency.
Disabling readiness and routing traffic before startup.
Treating larger timeouts as a substitute for correct probe semantics.
